title: Client speculative synthesis and structured checkpointing PRD (wip)
body:
Goal: explore a lightweight client-side speculative synthesis layer + structured checkpointing primitives from the Hosted API to reduce perceived latency and lower tool-call amplification for common flows (e.g., form-filling, code-edit suggestions, multi-step generation with small tool lookups).

Context / motivation:
- Hosted streaming + tool-calling is powerful but in many apps a large fraction of time is spent on tiny tool lookups or deterministic transformations (spellcheck, date normalization, contact lookup). Each tool call adds RTT and can multiply tokens/costs if done naively.
- SDKs can do some work locally (e.g., simple rules) but we need a safe way to let the client produce provisional outputs that are quickly verified or corrected by the server.
- Idea: define an opt-in speculative_synthesis + checkpointing protocol where the client can emit provisional structured fragments, which the server validates or replaces in-band. This keeps UX snappy, reduces round-trips for idempotent transforms, and keeps the canonical copy on the server.

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for server-side model decisions on open-ended content. Speculative synthesis only applies to small deterministic transforms or cached results.
- Not intended for bypassing safety or audit logs; all definitive outputs must be persisted/validated on the server.

User stories / scenarios:
1) Low-latency autofill in a CRM: client synthesizes a contact summary (from local cache) immediately, server validates contact id and canonical fields at a checkpoint; if mismatch, server emits a correction frame.
2) Code completions with quick local heuristics: local SDK proposes formatting and trivial code rewrites; server checkpoint either accepts unchanged or patches with more accurate tokens but only for changed spans.
3) Multistep generation with micro-tools: instead of immediately calling the address-normalization tool, client applies a deterministic normalization function and speculatively generates a normalized address; server checkpoint triggers a tool call only when divergence probability is high.

Requirements (high level):
- API primitives: speculative_synthesis=true (optional per-call flag); checkpoint frames with stable ids; patch operations (accept/replace/merge); delta sequence numbers for resume and reconciliation.
- Streaming semantics: partial frames can be streamed as "provisional-frame" events; server can later emit "checkpoint-accept" or "checkpoint-patch" referencing the frame id. Clients render provisional frames immediately but must be able to apply server corrections atomically when they arrive.
- Structured output: frames must carry a typed schema (e.g., json-schema id) so client can render/merge with minimal parsing. Server uses same schema to validate.
- Telmetry: divergence_rate per schema type (how often provisional vs final differ), average latency saved, % of avoided tool calls, cost delta.
- Safety/audit: all finalizations flow through server and are logged; provisional frames are ephemeral and flagged in payloads.

API sketch (proto-ish):
- Request body (JSON):
  {
    "model": "r-infer-small-v1",
    "input": "Generate contact summary",
    "speculative_synthesis": true,
    "checkpoint_schema": "https://schemas.redwood.ai/contact-v1",
    "max_provisional_age_ms": 3000
  }

- Streaming responses (newline-delimited events):
  - event: provisional-frame
    {"frame_id":"f_37","schema":"contact-v1","payload":{"name":"Sam"},"confidence_hint":0.98} // client can show this immediately
  - event: provisional-frame
    {"frame_id":"f_38","schema":"address-v1","payload":{"street":"123 Elm"},"confidence_hint":0.4} // low confidence -> client may show but with spinner
  - event: checkpoint-accept
    {"frame_id":"f_37","final":true,"canonical_id":"uid-293"} // server accepts frame f_37 as final
  - event: checkpoint-patch
    {"frame_id":"f_38","patch":{"street":"123 Elm St"},"reason":"normalization"} // apply patch atomically

SDK ergonomics (JS + mobile):
- Minimal API surface for app devs: renderProvisional(frame) + onCheckpoint(frameId, outcome) callbacks. Default SDK behavior: optimistic render + soft UI badge ("verifying...") until checkpoint.
- Client validators: SDK ships optional lightweight validators generated from the schema (e.g., type checks, regex checks). These run pre-render to avoid obviously invalid provisional frames.
- Backpressure and fallbacks: if client sees many low-confidence provisional frames, SDK can automatically trigger synchronous server-side tool calls (hedging) or show a reduced UI.
- Offline mode: clients can still synthesize provisional frames from local caches; these will reconcile later. Provide an idempotency token to avoid double-apply when network resumes.

Operational and product constraints:
- Rollout gating: start with internal beta customers and opt-in accounts. Monitor divergence_rate and user-visible reflow metrics before wider rollout.
- Metrics to monitor: provisional_accepted_rate, average_time_to_checkpoint, api_error_rate_for_checkpoints, %requests_with_provisional, per-schema divergence. Alert if divergence_rate > 5% on critical schemas.
- Cost model: checkpoint accept with no server change should cost less than a full tool chain; we should calculate unit economics (tokens + tool cost avoided) after initial trial.

Open questions (TODO):
- How do we represent complex merge semantics for overlapping patches (concurrent provisional frames)? CRDT-based? server-first strategy?
- What is the right confidence threshold model: client-provided hint vs server validation score?
- Can the checkpointing primitives be used for multi-client collaboration (two clients speculatively editing same session)? If so, need stronger ordering guarantees.
- How should we surface provisional frames in export/audit logs? Keep ephemeral by default but provide admin opt-in for traceability.

Rollout plan (sketch):
1) API + SDK experiment (internal only) – prototype basic flags + streaming checkpoint events; sample customers in CRM and IDE teams. 4 weeks.
2) Beta with 3 customers (GTM + Solution Eng enablement). Collect metrics, adjust schema ergonomics, refine default SDK behaviors. 6–8 weeks.
3) General availability: feature flags for customers + admin controls + documented cost model.

Developer notes / implementation hints:
- Server: keep provisional validation fast (schema checks, cache lookups) so checkpoints don't add much latency. Heavy validation (external tool call) should be asynchronous and use patch semantics when ready.
- SDK: provide small generated validators from schema registry (pick subset to run on mobile to keep bundle small).
- Observability: instrument per-frame lifecycle tracing (frame emitted -> checkpoint request -> accept/patch) to debug reflows.

Sample acceptance criteria (MVP):
- SDK renders provisional frames and applies server patches without full-page re-render in sample app.
- Provisional_accepted_rate > 80% for internal CRM schema (contact-v1) after 2 weeks.
- No customer-visible data-safety incidents; all final outputs must be logged and match server canonical versions.

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Sync with eng-serving-runtime to validate streaming event wire format (Diego).
- Spike: implement JS SDK validator generator for json-schema (Priya).
- Identify 2 customers for beta (solutions eng + GTM).
- Draft telemetry dashboard (metrics owner: Lucas).

Notes to self: keep this tightly scoped initially — target deterministic, low-risk transforms (normalization, canonical lookups). We can expand to probabilistic synthesis later if the metrics look good.

References / links (notes):
- Related: anticipatory-prefetch doc (see CONFLUENCE-1799) — overlaps but this PRD focuses on structured checkpoints rather than prefetch scheduling.
- Design sketches in figma: https://figma.com/redwood/provisional-ui (internal)
